title: GKE node bootstrap debug notes
content:
Context:
- Scratchpad for a flakey GKE node bootstrap issue observed on preemptible node pools (short lived, ~6-24h).
- Symptoms: node either never registers with control plane or registers then quickly becomes NotReady; pods stuck in ContainerCreating or CrashLoopBackOff. ClusterAutoscaler sometimes fails to scale down because node has non-daemonset pods that never evicted.

Commands I ran (chronological):
- gcloud compute ssh --zone=us-central1-b gke-redwood-xxxx-node-1 --project=redwood-prod \
  (checked /var/log/syslog and /var/log/messages)

- sudo journalctl -u kubelet --since "1h" --no-pager \
  <-- found repeated errors
  "Failed to register node \"gke-redwood-xxxx\" with API server: Post \"https://10.0.0.1:6443/api/v1/nodes\": dial tcp 10.0.0.1:6443: connect: connection refused"
  and later "kubelet: failed to load kubeconfig: open /var/lib/kubelet/kubeconfig: permission denied"

- sudo systemctl status kubelet \
  <-- shows active but with restart loops (RestartSec=5s); look at ExecStart preflight failures.

- cat /etc/default/kubelet /var/lib/kubelet/config.yaml \
  <-- noticed kubeletExtraArgs overridden by cloud-init script; --node-ip wrongly set to eth0 internal alias (was ephemeral and colliding)

- kubectl get nodes --all-namespaces --show-labels (from control plane) \
  <-- many NotReady nodes with taint node.kubernetes.io/unreachable:NoExecute for >5m

- kubectl describe node gke-redwood-xxxx-node-1 \
  <-- events: "KubeletNotReady: kubelet stopped posting node status" then "NodeAllocatableEnforced" messages.

- Check docker/containerd: sudo crictl ps -a; sudo systemctl status containerd \
  <-- container runtime sometimes in crash loop: "failed to start containerd: open /run/containerd/containerd.sock: connection refused"

- sudo ls -la /var/lib/kubelet/pki; sudo cat /var/lib/kubelet/kubeconfig \
  <-- kubeconfig either missing or owned by root:root with mode 600 (kubelet runs as root so should be fine) but kubelet complains about client certificate expired.

Error snippets collected: (copy-paste)
- "kubelet: client certificate has expired"
- "failed to register node: tls: failed to verify certificate: x509: certificate has expired or is not yet valid"
- "runtime network not ready: CNI plugin not initialized"
- "failed to create pod sandbox: networkPlugin cni failed to set up pod \"coredns-...\" network: failed to setup pod network: plugin staled: timed out"

Hypotheses / theories:
- Time drift: VM clock skew causing cert validation failures. (I saw drift on one node: date returned 1970-... once after resume).
- Preemptible VM resume paths break cloud-init ordering: kubelet starts before the GCE metadata server or CNI plugins have completed.
- Node provisioning script accidentally sets --node-ip to a secondary interface; API server rejects registration because NodeStatus uses unreachable IP.
- Token / cert rotation in GKE autopilot/dedicated gets out of sync when instances re-create quickly.
- Autoscaler interaction: cordon/drain not completing because eviction/force options conservative; poddisruptionbudgets blocking eviction.

Things I tried (with outcomes):
- sudo timedatectl set-ntp true; sudo systemctl restart systemd-timesyncd -> after sync, "client certificate expired" persisted until kubelet restarted and re-requested cert. Partial improvement.
- sudo systemctl restart kubelet -> sometimes node registers; sometimes kubelet immediately fails due to missing docker socket.
- sudo ip addr show; sudo ip route -> found eth0:1 alias earlier script created; removed alias and restarted kubelet -> node registered successfully (temporary).
- kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data --grace-period=30 --force -> in some cases pods stuck in Terminating because kube-proxy or CNI pods not evicted.
- helm upgrade --install calico calico/chart --wait -> CNI pods sometimes crash on install if kubelet not ready; ordering problem.
- gcloud compute instances reset <vm> -> VM reboot fixed networking on 2/4 nodes but not consistent.
- cluster-autoscaler logs: saw "no nodes are unneeded" / "node not autoscaled because pod has local storage" messages.

Root-cause candidates and evidence:
- Time sync seems strongly correlated (nodes with drift show TLS errors). Evidence: after forcing ntp sync, kubelet TLS errors drop.
- Cloud-init race: observed kubelet start before google-guest-agent had written metadata (kubelet config references metadata for CA). Could reproduce by booting instance with a heavy init script and checking service startup order.
- Preemptible resume path (GCE) sometimes loses ephemeral network interface naming, causing kubelet --node-ip mismatch.

Short-term mitigations tested:
- Add systemd drop-in to kubelet.service ExecStartPre to block until metadata server responds (curl -sS http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/instance/id -H "Metadata-Flavor: Google"). This reduced failed bootstraps in my small test.
- Bump kubelet restart backoff and add script to sleep until containerd socket exists.
- Patch cloud-init to not create eth0:1 alias.

Long-term asks / TODOs: (prioritized)
1) Add a gating healthcheck in the GKE node image to ensure time sync + metadata reachable + containerd socket present before enabling kubelet. (Owner: infra-image)
2) Review cluster-autoscaler settings regarding scale-down-delay and prefer to force-drain older preemptible nodes earlier. (Owner: platform-engineering)
3) Add Prometheus alert for kubelet TLS errors and node time skew > 5s. (Owner: observability)
4) Create a small e2e repro that boots a node with simulated slow metadata and ensure bootstrap ordering resilient. (Owner: eng-infrastructure)

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Is GKE-managed node auto-rotation involved? Check GKE release notes for "kubelet certs rotation" around the timeframe.
- Should we switch preemptible pools to use restart-on-failure rather than termination action to avoid weird resume states?
- Are any workloads using hostNetwork or hostPath that block node termination? Need to scan for pods without poddisruptionbudget or with local storage claims.

Quick checklist to run when a node is observed NotReady: (copy for on-call)
- ssh to node -> sudo timedatectl status; sudo ntpq -p
- sudo systemctl is-active containerd && sudo crictl ps -a
- sudo journalctl -u kubelet -n 200 --no-pager | tail -n 100 (look for cert/time/cni messages)
- cat /var/log/syslog | grep metadata && curl -s -H "Metadata-Flavor: Google" http://metadata.google.internal/computeMetadata/v1/instance/id
- ip addr show; ip route; check for unexpected aliases (eth0:1)
- kubectl describe node <node> -> events, lastHeartbeatTime, lastTransitionTime
- kubectl get pods --all-namespaces -o wide | grep <node> (identify blocking pods)

Notes for next run: try reproducing with a small GKE node pool of 3 preemptible instances with an extra 30s sleep in guest agent boot script to emulate slow metadata. Capture systemd startup order with systemd-analyze blame and journalctl -b -u kubelet.

Random snippets to keep:
- "If you see: client certificate has expired -> check system time and kubelet cert timeline. On GKE the node bootstrap may rely on metadata-issued certs that re-create after kubelet requests with correct time."
- "CNI late start kills pod readiness which prevents kubelet from moving to Ready state even if node registers."

End of scratchpad.

-- Ava M.
